body: You can use `std::size` here

I have some opinions on where to put these kinds of functions, but I think it's totally fine to park them here for the moment.
However, the first argument should be a `Span<char32_t>`, imo.
I kind of hesitated, because you have to construct a span to use it then, like that both string and span have the data to use it directly. But I could see taking a span too.
oh didn't know we were using it, will do. Thanks
Creating a span is as expensive as creating a pointer and size int - that is, pretty much free. We won't need to worry about that i think :)
It's more about simplicity of taking base types instead of a construct, not performance here. But as I said, If you prefer taking a span, that's ok for me.

I think I get it, but eventually I'd like to move a lot of `String` functions to `StringSpan` (or similar) to give callers the chance to avoid `String` entirely if it's not needed. There will probably be many more functions like this, and if they uniformly take `Span`, that would make it easier in the long run, I think.
Changed it to take a span instead.
This shouldn't need to allocate a `String`. However, my [equality operator PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104280) is still outstanding, so I think it's acceptable for the moment.
yeah, it would be better to not have to construct the string, but we can't right now. We can update this if your PR is merged.
Sorry to always make you look out for this stuff, I don't think I'll ever get used to it. Done, thanks.
